doc.title: Clyde Kerr Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006

title: Father's handwritten arrangements, lost in the storm, played in Chicago
summary: Father loved Ellington, Henderson and Lunceford and wrote arrangements; much was ruined by the flood, but one was played with Jon Faddis in Chicago.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Oh yeah man. It’s just crazy. But my father did a lot with big bands and he loved Duke Ellington, Fletcher Henderson and the Jimmie Lunceford band and he taught himself how to write music and arrange for big bands and some of his music was at my sister’s home in a shed that was outside and I had about a third of that in my home but that part of my house was all wiped out by the storm. She lived by the London Avenue Canal and when that water came over it just knocked it out. Not only the music but tapes, photos and albums and all of that stuff man. It’s like a life — and his thing was always hand written so it was like a monk in a monastery copying the scripture. He had a beautiful penmanship man. But I have some of his music. I went to Chicago in the first part of April and we played a couple of his — one of his, an original composition and
arrangement with the Chicago Jazz Ensemble with Jon Faddis. And they really loved it. He did some beautiful music man. I was blessed.
